_comment: security-ci suppressions (fail-closed). Each entry MUST carry: (1) exact identity via source_id OR tool+rule+path_contains (bare tool+rule is class-wide and rejected); (2) suppressing disposition in {accepted-false-positive,false-positive,remediated,risk-accepted,wont-fix} — deferred/open are ledger states and never suppress; (3) reason/rationale; (4) owner; (5) typed Security approval (owner or approved_by exactly security|sec|security-lead|sec-lead|security-team or those local-parts @domain — no substring spoofs); (6) non-expired expires (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetime). Malformed/expired/unauthorized rows never suppress and are logged ERROR. See scripts/security-ci-to-pulse.py::validate_allowlist_entry.

allowlist.reason: Intentional and required: the MCP servers bind 0.0.0.0 to be reachable across internal Docker/Tailscale networking (not public-facing; DNS-rebind protection is deliberately disabled for these internal services). Binding 127.0.0.1 would make them unreachable from other pods. PLAT-1562 (base.py), PLAT-1564 (pulse_server.py).
False positive: the flagged '0.0.0.0' literal is an entry in Django ALLOWED_HOSTS, not a socket bind. PLAT-1566.
false positive: test-only JWT fixture secret literal, not a runtime credential
false positive: test-only JWT key fixture literal, not a runtime credential
accepted workflow bootstrap: installs Trivy release binary inside the isolated CI job before scanning

Accepted false positive (adjudicated PLAT-3069, 2026-07-04, security-lead; recurs as PLAT-4551). python-multipart is NOT pinned in any manifest - it is a transitive dependency of `mcp` only; mcp-server/requirements.txt and pyproject.toml declare no python-multipart line, and dependency resolution installs a patched release (0.0.32+, above every listed fixed floor 0.0.18-0.0.31). No direct parser import/use in-repo. Re-remediate only if security-ci reports a concrete manifest pin below the fixed floor.
